output:
Hey Mikaela, sorry for the slow reply! Happy to give you the real version.

We’ve got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds, and started 10 in 7 on 21 September after mating had started. We skip Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday arvo milkings and Sunday arvo as well, so four once-a-days a week. Still up for the 5.15 morning milking every day unfortunately!

Going off the Fonterra app, milksolids are down about 6% compared with the same weeks last year. The rep had told us to expect 8–10%, so it hasn’t been as bad as we were braced for, but it’s still a real hit. Who knows how much of the difference is the milking pattern versus the season either.

Cells did jump. We were at 110,000 and went up to about 180,000 for the first three weeks. They’ve come back to around 135,000 now, so not mental but definitely something to watch. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you.

And the bad bit, because I’d hate to leave this out: we had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo. We didn’t spot her until the next morning and she lost a quarter. That was pretty awful, and a good reminder that the time off milking doesn’t mean you can stop keeping an eye on them.

The cows came round quicker than I thought they would. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine. Lameness has been way down too, which has been a big plus with our walk to the back paddocks being 1.8km. We’ve got four on the lame list now compared with 11 this time last year.

The hours have made the biggest difference for us. Kieran reckons it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October! And the first Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years. Felt very strange driving away but we got over it pretty quick 😂

Honestly I wouldn’t go back, the hours alone are worth the 6% to us. And if Tom’s knees are as bad as you say, I reckon those arvos off would help him more than anything. But that’s just how it’s gone here, not a promise it’ll be the same at your place, especially starting after Christmas.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th if you like. And give me a ring any time, much easier than texting!
